- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.75) and forecast is below recent high, adjust upward by 1–2% to capture momentum.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.75) and forecast is above recent low, adjust downward by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.
- Avoid forecasting sharp spikes in price after a recent dip — model tends to overshoot and lag recovery; reduce forecast slope after 3 consecutive downward moves.
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from -1 to +1 within 3 days), reduce forecast volatility and apply mean reversion toward 30-day moving average.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% in 2+ consecutive days, reduce next forecast by 1–3% to avoid overestimating upward momentum.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.5 → -0.5 → +0.5), apply a 1–2% downward bias to forecast to avoid overfitting to recent sentiment.
